strings.name: Albert Einstein
strings.summary: Einstein helped lay the foundations of modern physics. His special and general theories of relativity transformed ideas about time, space and gravity, while his work also advanced understanding of light quanta and Brownian motion. The 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics particularly recognized his law of the photoelectric effect. His academic career spanned Europe and the United States, where he settled after the Nazis came to power in 1933.
strings.coverageNote: Selected life events and major scientific contributions. The Nobel Prize year (1921) is distinguished from the year it was awarded (1922).
strings.facts.fact-01.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-02.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-02.value: Swiss Federal Polytechnic in Zurich; doctoral research at the University of Zurich
strings.facts.fact-03.label: Main research
strings.facts.fact-03.value: Relativity, statistical physics and quantum theory
strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Relativity
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Introduced special relativity in 1905 and completed a major formulation of general relativity in 1915.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Photoelectric effect and Nobel Prize
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Received the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics for contributions to theoretical physics, especially his discovery of the law of the photoelectric effect.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Dies in Princeton
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Died after many years of theoretical research in the United States, leaving a deeply influential body of work in physics.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Moves to the United States
strings.timeline.event-02.text: Left Germany after the Nazis took power and continued his theoretical physics research in Princeton.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Receives the 1921 Nobel Prize
strings.timeline.event-03.text: The award particularly recognized the law of the photoelectric effect; the prize for that year was awarded in 1922.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Presents general relativity
strings.timeline.event-04.text: Placed gravity within a new theory of spacetime, providing a foundation for modern gravitational research and cosmology.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Takes a position in Berlin
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Left Zurich for Berlin and joined Germany’s scientific research institutions.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Receives his first formal academic appointment
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Became an associate professor of theoretical physics at the University of Zurich, ending his period at the patent office.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Research in the “miracle year”
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Published work on light quanta, Brownian motion and special relativity, and submitted his doctoral thesis.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Joins the Bern patent office
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Continued independent research in physics while examining patent applications.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Begins studying in Zurich
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Began studying physics and mathematics at the Federal Polytechnic, completing his studies in 1900.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Born in Ulm
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Born in the German Empire; later studied and worked in several European cities.
